title: Postpartum Endometritis: Recognition, Antimicrobial Pathway and Escalation

evidenceAudit.scope: Women after childbirth with suspected endometritis or postpartum sepsis in the emergency department (ED), maternity unit or ward: recognition, blood cultures and lactate, antibiotics within 1 hour, source control for retained products or abscess, group A streptococcus (GAS) precautions and intensive care unit (ICU) referral. Uses the World Health Organization (WHO) 2015 recommendation, the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) Green-top Guideline 64b and product information.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-22.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi postpartum sepsis guideline was found.
WHO recommends clindamycin with gentamicin but the opened entry gives no doses; doses are from product information.
The RCOG suggested regimen table (Appendix 3) was garbled in the copy opened.
Breastfeeding compatibility of each antibiotic was not given in the opened sources; take microbiology and pharmacy advice.
Typical normal ranges for white cells and C-reactive protein are not from these sources.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: Postpartum endometritis is infection of the uterine lining after birth; it can progress to sepsis (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 7). Retained products of conception and prolonged rupture of membranes raise risk (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Table 1). Group A streptococcus can cause rapid, severe sepsis and spreads to contacts and the baby (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Sections 14 to 16). Infected retained tissue or abscess needs source control as well as antibiotics (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 13).

symptoms: Fever or feeling unwell after birth (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 7).
Offensive vaginal discharge; smelly suggests anaerobes, serosanguinous suggests streptococci (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Table 2).
Pain out of proportion to signs suggests deep infection (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 7).
physicalSigns: Pyrexia, hypothermia or tachycardia (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 7).
Uterine pain and tenderness, delayed uterine involution (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 10 and Table 2).
Hypotension and organ dysfunction in severe sepsis (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 13.5).
redFlags: Severe sepsis: intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 13.1).
Lactate 4 mmol/L or more: tissue hypoperfusion (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 12).
Shock or organ dysfunction: ICU admission (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 13.5).
Suspected GAS: isolate in a single room and give prophylaxis to the newborn (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Sections 14 and 15).
precipitants: Retained products of conception (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Table 1).
Prolonged spontaneous rupture of membranes (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Table 1).
Vaginal discharge before birth (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Table 1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Renal angle pain and urinary findings (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 10).
Wound signs or collection on imaging; drainage (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 13).
Breast signs; drainage of abscess (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 13).

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: The key investigation; take before antibiotics (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 12).

clinicalManagement.title: Recognise and sample
actions: Check temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, uterine tenderness and lochia (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 7 and Table 2).
Take blood cultures before antibiotics and measure lactate (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 12).

clinicalManagement.title: Start antibiotics
actions: Endometritis: clindamycin with gentamicin (see Medicines) (WHO 2015 endometritis recommendation; conditional, very low certainty).
Severe sepsis: piperacillin–tazobactam or a carbapenem plus clindamycin; add a glycopeptide if methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is suspected (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 13.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Control the source
actions: Image for retained products or abscess and arrange uterine evacuation or drainage (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Sections 12 and 13).

clinicalManagement.title: Escalate
actions: Admit to ICU for shock or organ dysfunction (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 13.5).

clinicalManagement.title: GAS precautions
actions: Isolate in a single room with en suite and use protective equipment (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 14).
Give antimicrobial prophylaxis to the newborn and warn close household contacts (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Sections 15 and 16).

regimens.indication: Postpartum endometritis or severe postpartum sepsis
regimens.dose: 600 mg to 1.2 g per day in 2 to 4 doses for serious infection; 1.2 to 2.7 g per day for more severe infection (Clindamycin SmPC, Section 4.2).
regimens.route: Intravenous infusion, diluted to 18 mg/mL or less, no faster than 30 mg per minute
regimens.duration: Until clinically improved, then review with microbiology
adjustments: Prolonged therapy: check liver and kidney function (Clindamycin SmPC, Section 4.2).
Breastfeeding limits some antimicrobials; take microbiology advice early (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 13.1).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Diarrhoea: consider Clostridioides difficile colitis (Clindamycin SmPC, Section 4.4).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to clindamycin or lincomycin (Clindamycin SmPC, Section 4.3).
Never as undiluted intravenous bolus (Clindamycin SmPC, Section 4.2).

adjustments: Renal impairment: reduce dose and adjust interval to creatinine clearance (Gentamicin SmPC, Section 4.2).

monitoring: Levels: peak not above 10 mg/L; trough not above 2 mg/L with divided dosing or 1 mg/L once daily (Gentamicin SmPC, Section 4.2).
Renal, hearing and balance function (Gentamicin SmPC, Section 4.4).

patientEducation: Infection of the womb after birth is treatable; report fever, smelly discharge or worsening pain.
Ask before breastfeeding while on new medicines.
Household members should report sore throat or fever if GAS is found.
lifestyleAndDiet: Rest, fluids and support with infant care during recovery.
mdtReferrals: Obstetrician; midwife; emergency physician; microbiology; anaesthesia and ICU; neonatal team for newborn prophylaxis in GAS.
dischargeCriteria: Afebrile and improving, source controlled, oral plan agreed with microbiology, newborn and contacts managed if GAS, follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Postnatal review after discharge; microbiology follow-up of cultures (RCOG GTG 64b 2012, Section 13.1).
